title: Diffusion Differentiable Resampling
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Our method's runtime scales gracefully and beats the costlier baseline across sample counts and tunable settings, with a clear crossover.
layout: 2 side-by-side log-scale line plots; left vs sample count, right dual x-axes
description: Two side-by-side black-and-white line plots on a log-scale y-axis labeled average time in seconds. The left panel plots time against number of samples N, from 2^7 to 2^13. It has four curves: solid lines for diffusion resampling with K=4 (cross markers) and K=32, and dashed lines for optimal transport (OT) with epsilon 0.8 (cross markers) and 0.1. All curves rise with N. Diffusion with K=4 is the lowest, and OT with epsilon 0.1 is the highest. The right panel fixes N=8192 and uses dual x-axes: time steps on the bottom and OT epsilon on top. Diffusion time rises with time steps as a solid line, and OT time falls as epsilon grows as a dashed line. The two lines cross near 2^4 time steps. Legends sit inside each panel, and the figure uses only line style and markers to distinguish methods.
caption: Average running times of diffusion resampling and OT.
abstract: This paper is concerned with differentiable resampling in the context of sequential Monte Carlo (e.g., particle filtering). Drawing on reparametrisation, we propose a new resampling method that is informative and instantly differentiable, based on a training-free diffusion model surrogate. We theoretically prove that our diffusion resampling method provides a consistent resampling distribution, and we show empirically that it outperforms the state-of-the-art differentiable resampling methods on multiple filtering and parameter estimation benchmarks. Finally, we show that it achieves competitive end-to-end performance when used in learning a complex dynamics-decoder model with high-dimensional image observations.
